{"content":"### Facts

1. The source describes a fictional benefits form.
2. The source contains no real resident data.
3. The title used by management, “inclusive launch,” states an ambition rather than a measured inclusion outcome.
4. No general accessibility certification was commissioned.
5. Reviewers sampled 80 of 640 message strings.
6. The sample contained 40 Spanish strings and 40 Polish strings.
7. All 80 sampled strings retained the glossary’s approved entitlement terms.
8. Six Spanish strings reversed the meaning of the deadline exception.
9. The Polish sample had no deadline reversal.
10. Terminology conformity and semantic correctness were separate checks.
11. Neither result certifies all 640 strings.
12. A second reviewer checked the six reversals and agreed.
13. The remaining strings did not receive that second semantic review.
14. An automated colour-contrast scan passed the three tested page templates.
15. Keyboard-only testing could not activate the document-upload button on the second template.
16. The upload defect was still open.
17. Screen-reader testing announced the upload label correctly on the second template.
18. Screen-reader testing did not test keyboard activation.
19. The source states that a visually correct label is not evidence that a keyboard user can upload a document.
20. Management approved a keyboard-fix proposal.
21. No deployed keyboard fix is recorded.
22. Task completion in the old English-only service was 33 of 50 moderated sessions.
23. The multilingual form recorded 42 completions in 50 unmoderated sessions.
24. Completion in the old service required a final submitted application.
25. The new dashboard counted reaching the review screen as completion.
26. Participants were recruited from different channels.
27. Participants were neither assigned randomly nor matched for prior experience.
28. The source states that the dashboard’s apparent improvement is not a comparable completion-effect estimate.
29. A preprocessing step called case folding normalised letter case.
30. Case folding did not merge benefit cases or applications.
31. Three runs on the same 80 strings flagged six, five, and six semantic issues with a sampling-based checker.
32. A human reference review identified the six deadline reversals.
33. The automated run counts do not establish three different ground truths or a stable checker.
34. The checker version was held fixed.
35. The checker’s sample order varied.
36. The appendix says legal approval covers the Spanish consent paragraph only.
37. The source gives no approval date.
38. The source gives no temporal relationship between the approval and the sample review.
39. Polish consent approval is not documented.
40. Translation availability does not itself establish legal approval.
41. The coordinator authorised a corrected-form usability study conditional on a verified upload fix.
42. The coordinator withheld general release.
43. The study budget includes translation fees.
44. The study budget excludes staff time.
45. No cost saving is demonstrated.
46. A separate satisfaction poll received 18 responses from 90 invitations.
47. Sixteen poll respondents said the wording was clearer.
48. The source says nonresponse and self-selection prevent treating that fraction as population satisfaction.
49. The poll did not measure successful submission or uptake of benefits.
50. The source says management’s “inclusive-launch” phrase should not be repeated as a finding.

### Interpretations

- None.

### Unknowns

- Whether the 560 unsampled strings contain the same or other terminology or semantic issues; the source says the sample results do not certify all 640 strings.
- Whether the form as a whole meets any general accessibility standard; no general accessibility certification was commissioned.
- Whether the upload defect was fixed after the recorded status; no deployed fix is recorded, and the source does not give a later status.
- Whether the approved keyboard-fix proposal was implemented.
- Whether task completion would differ under comparable completion definitions, recruitment, and participant assignment; the reported figures are not a comparable completion-effect estimate.
- Whether the checker would produce stable results on repeated runs; the source says the run counts do not establish a stable checker.
- Whether Polish consent received legal approval.
- The date of the stated Spanish consent approval and its timing relative to the sample review.
- Whether the poll’s 16-of-18 response fraction represents satisfaction in a wider population; the source explicitly rules out treating it as population satisfaction.
- Whether the form increased successful submissions or benefits uptake; the poll did not measure these outcomes.
- Whether the “inclusive launch” ambition was achieved as an inclusion outcome; the source says it is not a measured outcome.
- Reasons for withholding general release beyond the stated conditional authorization of a study and the requirement for a verified upload fix.
- Any cost saving from the study; none is demonstrated.
- The source does not establish a broad finding that the service is accessible or inaccessible. It reports specific test results, including a keyboard activation failure on one tested template.

### Development sequence

- Reviewers sampled 80 of 640 strings: 40 Spanish and 40 Polish. The source does not date this review.
- The sample checks recorded approved entitlement terms in all 80 strings, six Spanish deadline reversals, and no Polish deadline reversal. A second reviewer later checked and agreed with the six reversals; the remaining strings did not receive that second semantic review.
- The automated contrast scan passed three tested templates. Keyboard-only testing could not activate the upload button on the second template, and the defect was still open. Screen-reader testing announced the label correctly on that template but did not test keyboard activation. The source does not establish the chronology among these access checks.
- The task results reported for the old English-only service and the multilingual form use different completion definitions and different session formats. The source does not establish a comparable effect or causal relationship between the form and the difference in recorded figures.
- Three checker runs on the same 80 strings flagged six, five, and six issues; the checker version was fixed and sample order varied. The source does not establish that these counts are separate ground truths or demonstrate checker stability.
- The appendix states that legal approval covers the Spanish consent paragraph only; it gives no date or timing relative to the sample review. Polish consent approval is not documented.
- The coordinator authorised a corrected-form usability study conditional on a verified upload fix and withheld general release. The source does not establish a broader chronology or decision rationale beyond that stated condition.

### Editorial relevance

- Facts 3–4, 7–13, and 50 are relevant to the wording and inclusion claims.
- Facts 14–21 are relevant to the reported access checks and upload-button result.
- Facts 22–28 are relevant to the task-completion figures and their comparison limits.
- Facts 29–35 are relevant to the preprocessing definition and checker-run variation.
- Facts 36–45 are relevant to approval status, the follow-up study, release decision, and budget claim.
- Facts 46–49 are relevant to the poll and its measurement limits.
- The broad claim that the service is accessible, and any claim of measured inclusion or general service quality, is not established; see Unknowns."}
